  "article": "# The same six runes on LP2-27 and LP2-55\n\n**`ᛞᛄᚢ-ᛒᛖᛁ` appears once on each of these two pages.** The six runes are conventionally transliterated `DJU-BEI`; the hyphen is a visible separator and does not count as a rune. In the archived text they begin at rune offset **28 on LP2-27** and **70 on LP2-55**, counting from zero at the start of each page.\n\n![The same six-rune DJU-BEI sequence appears at zero-based offsets 28 and 70 on LP2-27 and LP2-55.](experiments/records/dju-bei-cross-page/offsets.svg)\n\n| Page | Where to look | Zero-based rune offset | One-based rune position | Exact source slice |\n| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | --- |\n| [LP2-27](#/reader/lp2-27) | line 2, columns 11–17 | 28 | 29 | `ᛞᛄᚢ-ᛒᛖᛁ` |\n| [LP2-55](#/reader/lp2-55) | line 4, columns 4–10 | 70 | 71 | `ᛞᛄᚢ-ᛒᛖᛁ` |\n\nThe offset counts only the 29 Gematria Primus runes. Spaces, hyphens, punctuation and row ends are skipped, but the page's rune order is preserved. The count resets at each page. Thus this verifies the two locations reported in the supplied discussion without relying on an ambiguous character count that includes separators.\n\nThe recurrence is a **source observation**, not a decryption. It does not show that the phrase is plaintext, that one page supplies a key to the other, or that it explains suppressed doublets. The match was already known before this audit, so we do not attach a chance probability to it. This record checks these two stored transcriptions only; it does not claim a manuscript-wide search or fresh adjudication against the page images.\n\nTo reproduce, run `python experiments/records/dju-bei-cross-page/run.py --check` from the repository or extracted experiment bundle. The [script](experiments/records/dju-bei-cross-page/run.py) reads the archived [LP2-27](data/pages/lp2-27.json) and [LP2-55](data/pages/lp2-55.json) page records, checks their rune counts, and verifies the stored [coordinate report](experiments/records/dju-bei-cross-page/results.json). Compare the [original LP2-27 image](images/lp2-27.jpg) and [LP2-55 image](images/lp2-55.jpg) if a proposed interpretation depends on the exact visual form or adjacent marks.\n",
  "article_path": "experiments/records/dju-bei-cross-page/article.md",
  "script_sha256": "535c67e5f16ad3d549980707de5dbc9dac88efc8234a2895c0e60bf25f0490f9",

      "path": "experiments/records/doublet-boundaries/boundaries.svg",
      "caption": "The 86 archived doublets split by intervening mark. Hyphen class includes one pair that also crosses a row wrap; classes are exclusive."

  ],
  "article": "# Where the 86 doublets cross a separator\n\nThe standard LP2-00–55 count removes non-runes within each page. That makes some equal runes neighbors in the filtered stream even when a hyphen or row break separates them in the archived text. This audit locates those pairs and tests the site's seven stored LP2 reviewed-text edits.\n\n**Sixty of the 86 pairs are directly adjacent rune characters.** Three have only a row-wrap marker between them, 22 cross a hyphen, and one crosses other punctuation. No doublet crosses an apostrophe alone or with a soft row wrap. These categories are exclusive: a hyphen plus row wrap counts in the hyphen row.\n\n![A bar and legend split the 86 equal-rune pairs by intervening marks: 60 contiguous, 3 row-wrap only, 22 hyphen and 1 other punctuation.](experiments/records/doublet-boundaries/boundaries.svg)\n\n| Intervening marks | Equal pairs | All rune pairs in that class | Rate |\n| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |\n| None: rune characters touch | 60 | 9,637 | 0.623% |\n| Row wrap only (`/`, CR/LF) | 3 | 388 | 0.773% |\n| Apostrophe, perhaps with wrap | 0 | 3 | 0% |\n| Hyphen, perhaps with wrap | 22 | 2,721 | 0.809% |\n| Other separator | 1 | 152 | 0.658% |\n| **All within-page filtered pairs** | **86** | **12,901** | **0.667%** |\n\nThe first three rows follow the site's published rune-token convention: slash row markers and physical line breaks are removed, and an internal apostrophe is allowed. Under that convention, **63 of 10,028 within-token pairs** match (0.628%). This is a transcription-based token definition, not an image-verified judgment that every such pair lies within a manuscript word. Conversely, the 22 hyphen-crossing doublets would disappear from a strictly word-internal doublet count. Rates across these groups are descriptive; the small row-wrap and apostrophe groups do not justify a mechanism claim.\n\n## What the stored corrections change\n\nThe current archive has separate LP2 reviewed-text layers for pages 05, 07, 11, 15, 35, 37 and 38. They alter notation marks but preserve the ordered rune stream. Applying all seven leaves the **86 pair identities and all five doublet category counts unchanged**. None of the stored punctuation changes falls between a doublet in a way that moves it to another class.\n\nThis answers a deliberately limited question. The other LP2 pages have no separate reviewed layer here. The seven layers are not a second complete independent transcription, and this experiment does not recheck 86 pairs against the original 2400×3600 scans. A new rune correction could change both pair identities and counts; a new separator correction could change the word-internal classification without changing 86.\n\nThe [full doublet guide](#/wiki/doublets) explains the 86-event count and provides source coordinates. The [transcription guide](#/wiki/transcription-checking?section=coverage) lists which pages have reviewed layers. The [short-lag profile](#/experiments/doublet-lag-profile) keeps the filtered within-page rule and compares equality at rune distances one through five. These analyses answer different questions.\n\nThe [EA frequency control](#/experiments/ea-frequency-control) asks a separate question: whether the 86 observed repeat positions are numerically plausible as plaintext EA under one exact running-sum equation. It uses decoded GP indices from solved pages rather than assigning English digraphs by eye.\n\nThe [placement audit](#/experiments/doublet-placement) asks whether the event positions cluster by page or sit unusually close together after preserving the number of available within-page edges.\n\n## Reproduce and inspect\n\nExtract the experiment ZIP without flattening folders. Python 3.12 and its standard library suffice:\n\n```text\npython experiments/records/doublet-boundaries/run.py --check\npython experiments/records/doublet-boundaries/check.py\n```\n\nThe producer records SHA-256 hashes for the alphabet, all 56 archived page texts, and the seven page records with reviewed layers. `results.json` lists every doublet by page, zero-based rune index, source character offsets, intervening marks and reviewed-layer classification. Run `--write` to regenerate the report and SVG. The independent checker extracts runes with a separate regular-expression path, recounts separator classes, and checks all 86 offsets against the existing source-location ledger. That verifies the archived data handling; it does not authenticate the photographed glyphs.\n",

    "representation": "Archived rune transcription, filtered to the 29 GP glyphs; pages treated independently.",
    "procedure": "Apply three fully specified forward edits to all 56 page streams; count adjacent equality and length; enumerate every length-1–5 string over a three-rune toy alphabet to test inversion even with original length known.",
    "parameters": "Collapse each maximal equal run; insert fixed F on each original equal edge; insert the cyclic next GP rune on each original equal edge. Source attachment SHA-256 and all fixed rules in plan.json.",

  "outcome": "supported",
  "finding": "All three declared edits suppress repeats mechanically: 86→0 by deletion, 86→8 by fixed F insertion, and 86→0 by a nonmatching filler. The forward outputs can have multiple known-length inputs, so reverse recovery needs additional rules.",
  "limitations": "Applying edits to the already-sparse LP2 ciphertext does not show how the manuscript was encrypted. The nonmatching filler is an explicit control, not a documented historical glyph rule. Toy-alphabet ambiguity is a proof of non-injectivity, not an LP2 candidate count.",
  "next_steps": "Any claimed decryption must freeze the prior cipher stage, edit positions or filler policy, and decoding rule; verify exact recovery on planted known readings before trying unsolved text.",

  "visuals": [
    {
      "path": "experiments/records/doublet-collision-edits/collision-edits.svg",
      "caption": "Three declared forward collision edits suppress the 86 observed adjacent repeats while changing length by 86 symbols."
    }
  ],
  "article": "# Removing or splitting adjacent repeats\n\n**Result.** Three fixed edits all suppress adjacent repeats when applied as a final operation to the archived LP2-00–55 rune stream. They do **not** reveal which edit, if any, was used to make that stream. Both insertion rules can also give the same output from different inputs, even if the decoder knows the input length. A reverse-edit step therefore needs extra information that the proposal did not supply.\n\n![The original stream has 86 adjacent repeats. Deleting the later rune leaves none; inserting fixed F leaves eight; inserting a different rune leaves none.](experiments/records/doublet-collision-edits/collision-edits.svg)\n\nThe supplied list proposed deleting one copy of a repeat (`ABBC → ABC`) or splitting it with a filler (`ABBC → ABDBC`). We pinned one complete pass for each, plus a deliberately stronger insertion control. They are three **variants of one collision-edit idea**, not three independent LP2 decryptions.\n\n| Forward edit on LP2-00–55 | Runes afterward | Adjacent repeats afterward |\n| --- | ---: | ---: |\n| Original archive | 12,956 | 86 |\n| Collapse each run to its first rune | 12,870 | 0 |\n| Put `F` between each original repeat | 13,042 | 8 |\n| Put the next GP rune between each original repeat | 13,042 | 0 |\n\nThe eight repeats left by fixed `F` insertion occur where the original repeated rune is itself `F`; an `F` inserted between two `F`s does not separate them. Choosing a filler guaranteed to differ from the repeated rune removes that edge case, but this adaptive choice was **our control rule**, not a specified historical key. These are forward edits to an already sparse ciphertext. Reaching zero doublets by editing it says little about how its original 86 arose.\n\n## Why undoing an edit is harder\n\nThe deletion rule loses positions. For instance, the three four-rune strings `FFFTH`, `FFTH TH` and `FTH TH TH` (spaces here only separate GP rune labels) all collapse to `FTH`. Knowing there were four runes does not choose among them.\n\nInsertion can also be ambiguous, even with a declared filler. Under the fixed-`F` rule, `TH F TH TH` and `TH TH F TH` both become `TH F TH F TH`. Exhaustive enumeration over the small alphabet `{F, U, TH}`, holding original length fixed, first finds **two** ambiguous outputs among length-four originals for each insertion rule. That toy result proves these fixed transforms are not generally one-to-one; it does not estimate how many LP2 readings they permit. The [complete preimage counts](experiments/records/doublet-collision-edits/results.json) cover original lengths one through five.\n\nThe source example also mentions moving a repeated rune (`ABBC → ABCB`), but it does not say how to handle the end of a stream, runs longer than two, or new collisions. We have not turned that open rule into an invented test. Likewise, the filler glyph, the stage at which editing happens, and a decoder's removal clock were not fixed in the source.\n\n## Exact scope and next test\n\nWe filtered the [archived LP2 page texts](#/reader/lp2-00) to GP runes and edited each of the 56 pages separately. Page breaks never become adjacent pairs. The [plan](experiments/records/doublet-collision-edits/plan.json) states the pass order and run handling; [results](experiments/records/doublet-collision-edits/results.json) give the before/after count on every page. The original supplied discussion is identified by its attachment SHA-256 in the plan.\n\nA proposed LP2 decryption using one of these edits would need a frozen preceding cipher, filler or deletion-position rule, and a way to recover a planted known reading before scoring unsolved text. The [decoder controls](#/experiments/decoder-skip-controls) show why a plausible-looking output is not enough to establish exact recovery.\n\nRun from the repository root or the experiment ZIP with Python 3.12 or later:\n\n```text\npython experiments/records/doublet-collision-edits/run.py --check\npython experiments/records/doublet-collision-edits/check.py\npython experiments/records/doublet-collision-edits/plot.py --check\n```\n\nThe independent checker reconstructs edits by maximal equal-rune runs instead of the producer's adjacent-pair loop. It checks all page totals, input hashes, and toy preimage counts. Neither program treats a reduced doublet count as a plaintext reading.\n",
  "article_path": "experiments/records/doublet-collision-edits/article.md",

  "article": "# What surrounds the 86 ciphertext doublets?\n\nThe [doublet guide](#/wiki/doublets?section=ea-constraint) describes one proposed equation in which a repeated ciphertext rune would mark a plaintext EA. That statement is easy to overread. It fixes the **plaintext symbol at a transition** under the equation; it does not say that the repeated *ciphertext* rune is the EA rune, or that the neighboring ciphertext runes should spell an English word. This experiment records those local ciphertext values and asks whether they have extra ordering structure under a declared conditional control.\n\n![Counts of all 29 ciphertext symbols at the 86 doublet positions, compared with means from fixed-mask within-page permutations.](experiments/records/doublet-context/context.svg)\n\n## What the equation predicts\n\nFor `Cᵢ = Cᵢ₋₁ + Kᵢ(Pᵢ − 28) mod 29` with nonzero `Kᵢ`, `Cᵢ = Cᵢ₋₁` if and only if `Pᵢ = 28` (EA). The doublet's visible rune is `Cᵢ`, the **current ciphertext state**. It can be any of the 29 runes. A doublet on AE does not make AE the proposed plaintext; a doublet on EA does not offer special confirmation.\n\nIf the *following* plaintext rune is not EA and its key is independently uniform on 1–28, its difference `Cᵢ₊₁ − Cᵢ` is uniform on those 28 nonzero residues. The next ciphertext rune is then uniform over the 28 symbols **other than** `Cᵢ`. It is not independent of `Cᵢ` in absolute symbol terms, because equality is forbidden. If the following plaintext is EA, the next difference is zero and a triple results. The observed doublet mask has no consecutive zeros, so this record cannot use a fixed-mask control to judge how surprising that absence is.\n\n## The actual local inventory\n\nFrom the archived LP2-00–55 text, filter to the 29 GP runes, keep headings, and compare neighbors only within pages. This gives **86 zero differences in 12,901 transitions**. Each event is recorded by page and zero-based rune index in the [result ledger](experiments/records/doublet-context/results.json). One event has no preceding within-page difference; one has no following one. None has a zero difference immediately beside it. The remaining 85 preceding and 85 following differences are tabulated separately in all 28 nonzero residues.\n\nThe event-symbol counts range from **0 to 7**, rather than 3 to 7. GP index 17 (B) has no event; index 25 (AE) has seven; index 28 (EA) has three. The latter labels are ciphertext symbols, not decoded plaintext. Across all 29 bins there are **123 pairs of events sharing the same ciphertext symbol**. The local before-versus-after residue imbalance, defined in the [plan](experiments/records/doublet-context/plan.txt), is **27.786**. Both summaries were selected before this control was run, but the underlying doublet observation had already been seen.\n\n## A control that holds the known anomalies fixed\n\nFor each page, retain its first ciphertext rune, the positions of all zero differences and the multiset of all nonzero differences. Shuffle only the nonzero difference order within that page, then cumulatively add the differences modulo 29 to rebuild a synthetic ciphertext page. This preserves the **86-event mask exactly** and also preserves each page's difference histogram. It asks whether *placement relative to those zeros* adds anything beyond those known properties. It does not simulate English, a key generator, or the chance of obtaining 86 zeros in the first place.\n\n| Diagnostic | Observed | Central 95% of 5,000 conditional permutations | Trials at least observed |\n| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |\n| Same-symbol pairs among doublet events | 123 | 108–150 | 2,950 / 5,000 |\n| Before/after difference imbalance | 27.786 | 12.745–34.259 | 854 / 5,000 |\n\nBoth observed values sit inside these conditional ranges. In the figure, blue bars are the complete observed 29-symbol inventory and red ticks are the average count for each bin across the permutations. The ticks are not 29 separate significance cutoffs. The report also includes all 28 before and after residue bins, every event location, the seed (`330122`), and both inclusive rank directions.\n\nThis is **not independent corroboration** of the earlier [nonzero-difference histogram](#/experiments/ea-difference-independence). The same source differences are reused, and the new control deliberately fixes their pagewise histograms. The broad question “are these 86 positions really plaintext EA?” remains unanswered. A proposed key schedule would have to predict something further that can be checked without freely choosing plaintext neighbors after seeing the ciphertext.\n\n## Do hyphen-crossing doublets have different neighbors?\n\nThe [boundary ledger](#/experiments/doublet-boundaries) classifies **22** doublets as crossing a hyphen, **63** as within a rune token under the site's rule, and **one** as crossing other punctuation. The last event is kept in the [complete companion ledger](experiments/records/doublet-context/boundary-context.json) but excluded from this two-group comparison. Calling all 64 non-hyphen events “within-word” would misclassify that one event; even the 63-token group is a transcription convention, not a fresh image review.\n\nFor a repeated ciphertext rune at position `i`, the immediately preceding rune is at `i−2` and the following rune at `i+1`, if those positions exist within the same page. The table counts **ciphertext** GP labels. Circular distance means the smaller of the two distances between their indices around the 29-symbol alphabet; it does not measure English-letter similarity.\n\n| Doublet group | Events | Before available / distinct labels | Mean before distance | After available / distinct labels | Mean after distance |\n| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |\n| Hyphen-crossing | 22 | 22 / 16 | 5.95 | 22 / 17 | 8.23 |\n| Within-token | 63 | 62 / 25 | 8.06 | 62 / 25 | 7.87 |\n| Other separator, excluded from comparison | 1 | 1 / 1 | 2.00 | 1 / 1 | 5.00 |\n\nThere is a visible difference in the *mean preceding circular distance*, but that summary was inspected after this question arose. For a broader comparison fixed in the [companion plan](experiments/records/doublet-context/boundary-context-plan.json), we sum the two-group Pearson association scores over all 29 before-rune labels and all 29 after-rune labels, retaining a separate category for a missing page-edge neighbor. The observed score is **51.321**. We then keep every observed before/after context vector intact and permute which 22 of the 85 eligible events carry the hyphen label. In **6,495 of 10,000** global shuffles the score is at least this large; the central 95% of shuffled scores is **39.592–71.390**. A second control preserves each page's hyphen count and yields **8,626 of 10,000** at least as large, with a central range of **46.195–75.474**. Only **13 pages and 40 events** have labels that can move in that stricter control.\n\nThese are exploratory conditional ranks, not prospective p-values or a test that the 22 marks were placed randomly. The 22-event group is small, many labels are sparse, and page layout can affect both boundary status and ciphertext context. The whole-label statistic does not stand out under either stated comparison; it does not rule out a particular word-boundary cipher rule. In the proposed EA-stalling equation, the runes around a doublet remain ciphertext states. They cannot be compared directly with English words containing EA without a separately fixed key and boundary clock.\n\n## Reproduce and limits\n\nExtract the experiment ZIP without flattening it, then run:\n\n```text\npython experiments/records/doublet-context/run.py --check\npython experiments/records/doublet-context/check.py\npython experiments/records/doublet-context/boundary_context.py --check\n```\n\nThe producer reruns all 5,000 seeded conditional permutations and checks the saved JSON and SVG byte for byte. The separate checker re-extracts the Runic Unicode block, recomputes all 86 event locations and both diagnostics, and verifies each source hash. The companion script hashes both source ledgers, joins all 86 events by page and rune position, verifies neighboring runes against the archived page text, and reruns both 10,000-draw boundary-label controls. This checks the archived text, not a fresh image transcription. Neither control nor the exact algebra identifies the cipher, and these exploratory ranks are not adjusted for the wider history of questions asked of the same 86 events. See the [boundary audit](#/experiments/doublet-boundaries) and [placement audit](#/experiments/doublet-placement) for other, non-interchangeable scopes.\n",
  "article_path": "experiments/records/doublet-context/article.md",
  "script_sha256": "21b3bb14818a8ba8a96b9b1949818af153e1abfd840a8856ef08b9189072790d",

  }

  "article": "# Distances between doublet events\n\nThe proposal asks whether repeated runes, extracted in manuscript order, form a patterned sequence of their own. This recount finds **10 forward +4 differences at lag three, out of 83 comparisons (12.05%)**. It does not reproduce the reported 12.9%, and it does not verify the proposed p-value.\n\n“Not supported” refers to reproducing the exact numerical claims with these inputs and rules. It does not mean that every doublet-based cipher has been tested or rejected.\n\n## What is an event?\n\nRead LP2-00–55 in numerical order, including headings. Retain only the 29 alphabet runes within each page. Count overlapping adjacent equal pairs: AAA contributes two A events. Never create an event across a page boundary. Then join the extracted events in page order. The result is 86 events.\n\nAt lag one, compare each event with the next; at lag three, compare it with the event three places later. For example, in an event sequence A, B, C, D, the first lag-three comparison is A to D. This lag measures **event positions**, not rune positions or page distance.\n\nThe [short rune-lag profile](#/experiments/doublet-lag-profile) instead compares positions in the original rune streams before extracting doublets. Its lag-three denominator is 12,791 rune pairs, not the 83 event pairs counted here.\n\nFor indices a and b, the directed difference is `(b-a) mod 29`. The circular distance is the smaller of that difference and its reverse. Thus +4 and −4 share circular distance 4 but occupy different directed bins, 4 and 25. The proposed +4 claim is directional.\n\n## Complete comparison\n\n| Event lag | Comparisons | Cross-page comparisons | Mean circular distance | Forward +4 | Circular distances 5, 12 or 14 |\n| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |\n| 1 | 85 | 41 | 734/85 ≈ 8.6353 | 2 | 31 |\n| 2 | 84 | 63 | 52/7 ≈ 7.4286 | 1 | 22 |\n| 3 | 83 | 75 | 626/83 ≈ 7.5422 | 10 | 14 |\n\nThe earlier proposed lag-one mean was 8.81. These inputs instead give 8.6353. The exact reason for the difference cannot be determined without the original event list and counting implementation. The stored output includes all events and every comparison so a future comparison can locate the first divergence.\n\nPage boundaries matter here: 75 of 83 lag-three comparisons cross them. Resetting the comparisons at page boundaries would answer a different question; it is not an interchangeable implementation detail.\n\n## What should the +4 baseline be?\n\nUnder a uniform shuffle of this fixed event multiset, the exact probability of a forward +4 difference between distinct positions is **8/215 ≈ 3.7209%**. It is not exactly 1/29, because these event symbols have unequal frequencies. For counts c(a), sum `c(a) × c((a+4) mod 29)` over all a and divide by `86 × 85`.\n\nThis probability is an expectation for a single ordered comparison. Multiplying it by 83 gives the expected lag-three count, approximately 3.0884. It is **not** the probability of observing ten or more matches: comparisons share events, and a binomial independence assumption is not justified by this calculation.\n\nNo permutation tail probability is calculated here. Selecting +4, lag three, or the group of distances 5, 12 and 14 after inspecting data introduces selection choices. A later significance test must state which choices it addresses. See [null models](#/wiki/null-models) and [search space](#/wiki/search-space).\n\n## Reproduce and inspect\n\nExtract the experiment ZIP with its folders intact. No packages, network access or AI service are required.\n\n```text\npython experiments/records/doublet-event-lags/run.py --check\npython experiments/records/doublet-event-lags/check.py\n```\n\nThe producer uses the included doublet extractor and prints fresh JSON without `--check`. The independent checker uses overlapping regular-expression matches on the archived rune text, then checks every event, lag pair, histogram, distance and boundary flag. It also computes shuffle expectations from symbol frequencies instead of enumerating pairs of event positions.\n\nThese checks establish agreement about the archived transcription. They do not independently settle ambiguous handwriting. The [doublet guide](#/wiki/doublets) explains the source rules and supplies the original pair coordinates.\n\n## Read and reproduce the figure\n\nThe figure shows every possible forward difference, including bins with zero occurrences. Dark bars count within-page comparisons; pale bars count cross-page comparisons. The ten +4 matches split into **three within-page and seven cross-page** comparisons. These counts have different opportunities: only eight lag-three comparisons stay within a page, while 75 cross pages. Comparing raw bar lengths alone would overlook that imbalance.\n\nBrown marks show the expected total count per bin after shuffling the fixed multiset of 86 events. They are not confidence limits or a cutoff for significance. The chart does not assign separate null expectations to the two boundary groups.\n\nThe SVG is included in the download. To regenerate a figure, install Matplotlib in your Python environment, then run:\n\n```text\npython experiments/records/doublet-event-lags/plot.py --output my-distribution.svg\n```\n\nThe script refuses to overwrite an existing file. The numerical producer and independent checker still require only the standard library; plotting is optional.\n",

  "article": "# Do the reported doublet-event patterns survive better controls?\n\nAn earlier report extracted repeated adjacent runes from unsolved LP2 and described large GP distances between consecutive doublet symbols, concentrations at distances 5, 12 and 14, and a forward +4 difference at event lag three. The [event recount](#/experiments/doublet-event-lags) pins the 86-symbol sequence and finds a lag-one mean of 734/85 ≈ 8.635, rather than the reported 8.81. This companion record checks the reported patterns against two different shuffle controls. Neither control simulates a cipher; both ask what ordering could arise while holding specified aspects of the observed event inventory fixed.\n\n![Two histograms compare the observed lag-one distance sum of 734 with global and within-page event shuffles.](experiments/records/doublet-event-shuffle/shuffle-controls.svg)\n\n## Inputs and fixed statistics\n\nThe input is the exact [86-event ledger](experiments/records/doublet-event-lags/results.json) from LP2-00–55. Each event represents one adjacent equal-rune pair. For runes with indices *a* and *b*, the forward difference is `(*b* − *a*) mod 29` and the minimum circular distance is `min(d, 29 − d)`. Event lag counts places in this extracted list, not places in the manuscript. Event comparisons may cross a page boundary; doublets themselves were found only within pages.\n\nThe three source-specified measurements are the lag-one circular-distance sum **734** over 85 pairs, **31** lag-one distances in bins 5, 12 or 14, and **10** forward +4 matches among 83 lag-three pairs. We compare them with 20,000 seeded shuffles of the 86-event multiset. In a second control, each page retains its own event symbols and event count, but their order within that page is shuffled. The latter tests whether the apparent signal is largely due to different pages containing different sets of doublet runes.\n\n| Source-specified statistic | Observed | Global shuffle: draws ≥ observed | Within-page shuffle: draws ≥ observed |\n| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |\n| Lag-one circular-distance sum | 734 | 31 / 20,000 | 3,910 / 20,000 |\n| Lag-one distances 5, 12 or 14 | 31 | 5 / 20,000 | 879 / 20,000 |\n| Lag-three forward +4 | 10 | 13 / 20,000 | 23 / 20,000 |\n\nThe middle 95% of the global-shuffle lag-one sum is **545–694**; for within-page shuffles it is **648–767**. The observed 734 falls inside the latter interval. Therefore the broad “doublet events are farther apart” observation depends strongly on whether page-specific rune inventories are preserved. The +4 count stays unusual under these two narrow controls, but it was noticed after inspecting the data.\n\n## Selection matters\n\nThe source report singled out lag three and +4, as well as a set of three circular-distance bins. For a more realistic post-selection check, each shuffle can choose its own largest directed-difference bin from **all 29 bins at lags one through three**, and its own largest three-bin circular-distance total over those lags. The observed maxima are 10 and 31, respectively.\n\n| After allowing that choice | Global shuffle: draws ≥ observed | Within-page shuffle: draws ≥ observed |\n| --- | ---: | ---: |\n| Largest directed bin at any of lags 1–3 | 1,123 / 20,000 | 3,510 / 20,000 |\n| Largest three circular-distance bins at any of lags 1–3 | 4,434 / 20,000 | 9,653 / 20,000 |\n\nThis correction covers **only** those stated choices. It cannot account for all distances, statistics, transcriptions, page subsets or ideas someone may have considered before reporting a pattern. Thus the narrow +4 result should be treated as a lead for a prediction on untouched data, not as a cipher finding. The original report's permutation p-values cannot be reproduced exactly without its event list, implementation and randomization policy; these are new seeded calculations on the archived transcription.\n\n## Reproduce\n\nRun `python experiments/records/doublet-event-shuffle/run.py --check` to regenerate all 40,000 shuffles and verify every saved count. `check.py` independently recounts the three observed statistics from the pinned event ledger and checks the published Monte Carlo denominators. The [plan](experiments/records/doublet-event-shuffle/plan.json), [complete results](experiments/records/doublet-event-shuffle/results.json) and figure script are included in the experiment download. Tail estimates use `(count + 1) / (20,000 + 1)`; a small Monte Carlo fraction is not a probability that any proposed decryption is true.\n",

    {
      "path": "experiments/records/doublet-lag-profile/profile.svg",

  "article": "# Equal-rune pairs at distances one through five\n\nThe 86 neighboring equal-rune pairs are unusual under a count-preserving page shuffle. **The same deficit does not continue through lags 2–5** under this particular reference model. This narrows the observation: it concerns adjacency, rather than a blanket avoidance of repeating a rune within five positions.\n\n## Exactly what was compared\n\nFor each archived LP2-00–55 page, retain the 29 alphabet runes in order, including headings, and remove other characters. At lag *d*, compare rune *i* with rune *i + d* for every position that fits. Pairs may cross a word or line break after filtering; none cross a page boundary. LP2-50 contributes no rune pairs. A lag is measured in **rune positions**, not in the sequence of extracted doublet events used in the [event-lag experiment](#/experiments/doublet-event-lags).\n\n| Rune lag | Equal pairs | Pairs compared | Page-shuffle expected | Central 95% of 2,000 shuffles |\n| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |\n| 1 | 86 | 12,901 | 439.17 | 398–480 |\n| 2 | 435 | 12,846 | 437.29 | 396–479 |\n| 3 | 434 | 12,791 | 435.42 | 396–476 |\n| 4 | 451 | 12,736 | 433.55 | 392–472 |\n| 5 | 463 | 12,681 | 431.68 | 391–469 |\n\n![Five horizontal rows show observed equal-rune pair counts against the page-shuffle central ranges. Lag one is far left of its range; lags two through five lie within theirs.](experiments/records/doublet-lag-profile/profile.svg)\n\nThe dark dot is the observed count, the pale band is the middle 95% of seeded shuffles, and the thin mark is the exact expected count. The band is a visual reference for one shuffle model, not a general confidence interval for possible ciphers. Lag five sits near its upper edge; its 463 matches were met or exceeded in 109 of the 2,000 shuffles. This is not a basis for selecting lag five as a discovery after seeing the chart.\n\n## Why the shuffle expectation changes with lag\n\nFor a page with *n* runes and symbol counts *c*, any pair of distinct positions matches with probability `Σ c(c−1) / [n(n−1)]` after uniformly shuffling that page. A lag *d* supplies `max(n−d, 0)` pairs. Multiply and sum over pages to get the exact expected count shown above. The denominator falls as the lag grows; the expectation therefore changes even when the per-pair shuffled probability is the same.\n\nEach of the 2,000 trials independently permutes the filtered runes **within each page**, preserving the page lengths and rune frequencies. It does not simulate English, a running-sum cipher, or a key process. None of those trials had as few as 86 lag-one matches, but `0/2,000` only bounds what this Monte Carlo run observed. The [uniform additive-key record](#/experiments/uniform-additive-doublets) supplies an exact probability for a different, more restrictive model; its tail should not be transferred to this shuffle model.\n\nThe observed contrast is compatible with several mechanisms: a rule that avoids immediate repeats, a plaintext/cipher relation that makes adjacent repeats rare, or preprocessing that alters adjacent symbols. It does not identify which one applies. Also, lags 2–5 were selected after the adjacency anomaly was known. The shaded bands are descriptive and unadjusted for multiple looks.\n\nThis profile filters out the separators between runes. The [boundary audit](#/experiments/doublet-boundaries) shows that 26 of the 86 adjacent equal-rune pairs have an intervening row wrap or punctuation mark in the archived text.\n\n## Reproduce\n\nExtract the experiment download without flattening folders. Python 3.12 and its standard library suffice:\n\n```text\npython experiments/records/doublet-lag-profile/run.py --check\npython experiments/records/doublet-lag-profile/check.py\n```\n\nThe producer records SHA-256 hashes of all 56 page texts and the index. Run `--write` to regenerate the stored JSON and SVG. The second script independently extracts Runic Unicode characters with a regular expression, recounts each lag and derives the exact shuffle expectations. The JSON includes exact fractional expectations, shuffle intervals, counts on either side of each observed result, seed and quantile convention. This is a transcription-based analysis; it does not resolve disputed glyph readings in the source photographs. For the complete 86-event ledger and the algebraic EA proposal, see [the doublet guide](#/wiki/doublets).\n",
  "article_path": "experiments/records/doublet-lag-profile/article.md",

  "record_type": {

  "visuals": [
    {
      "path": "experiments/records/doublet-placement/placement.svg",
      "caption": "Observed page and position metrics (dots) compared with the middle 95% of 10,000 length-aware placements of 86 events (bands); see the record for the second page-count-fixed reference."
    }
  ],
  "article": "# Are the 86 doublets clustered by page or position?\n\nThe low overall doublet count is established for the archived LP2-00–55 rune streams. A separate question is where the 86 surviving equal-neighbor events fall. This record compares their locations with **two explicitly conditional placement controls**, so a short page is not treated as if it offered as many opportunities as a long one.\n\n![Observed zero-doublet pages, page-count variance, shortest event gap and page-edge events shown against length-aware random-placement ranges.](experiments/records/doublet-placement/placement.svg)\n\n| Measurement | Observed | Fixed-total placement: central 95% | Fixed-page-count placement: central 95% |\n| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |\n| Pages with no doublet | 13 of 55 | 8–17 | Fixed at 13 |\n| Page-count variance / mean | 1.204 | 0.715–1.483 | Fixed at 1.204 |\n| First or last five within-page edge slots | 4 | 1–8 | 1–8 |\n| Shortest gap between event starts | 6 runes | 1–7 | 1–6 |\n| Median gap | 113 runes | 81–127 | 83–117 |\n| Gaps of five runes or less | 0 | 0–6 | 0–6 |\n\nAn event occupies the left edge index of an equal adjacent rune pair. The input has **12,901 available within-page edges** on 55 nonempty pages; LP2-50 has no alphabet runes. For gap measurements, place the filtered page streams one after another in LP2 numerical order and subtract the starting rune coordinates of consecutive events. The resulting 85 gaps include comparisons across page boundaries, but no *event* is created across a page boundary. The shortest actual gap is six runes, on LP2-27. “Gap” here is a distance between event starts, not the [alphabet distance between extracted doublet symbols](#/experiments/doublet-event-lags).\n\n## Why 13 empty pages is not itself surprising\n\nUnder the first control, choose 86 distinct edge slots uniformly from all 12,901 available slots. This keeps the observed total and the actual page lengths but lets each page's event count vary. Using each page's length, the exact expected number of nonempty pages with **zero** events is **12.25**. Ten thousand seeded placements yielded a central range of 8–17; the observed 13 sits inside. The raw count variance-to-mean ratio is 1.204, likewise inside its length-aware range. Shorter pages have fewer chances to contain an event, so a crude equal-length Poisson comparison would answer a different question.\n\nThe 13 zero-doublet pages are LP2-05, 07, 13, 14, 15, 17, 28, 31, 37, 38, 40, 49 and 53. Their mean rune length is 214, versus about 242 for the 42 pages with at least one event. The complete output lists every page's length, count and event index. This difference in means is descriptive; the length-aware placement result is the relevant control for the zero-page count. No page style or section classification is inferred from these numbers.\n\n## Are neighboring events kept apart?\n\nWith the total-only placement control, the minimum gap reaches six or more in **540 of 10,000** trials. With the second control, which keeps each page's observed doublet count fixed and randomizes only its event positions, it does so in **451 of 10,000** trials. The absence of gaps one through five is therefore near the edge of both reference distributions, while the median gap of 113 and the four events in the first or last five edge slots lie within their central ranges.\n\nThese tail fractions are exploratory. The minimum-gap observation was already known when these controls were chosen, and a uniformly selected set of edge slots does not reproduce every way a rune stream can make overlapping equal pairs. Natural-language EA positions, punctuation policy and a real key schedule could each alter gap behavior. The controls help specify a future mechanism test; they do not identify one.\n\n## Reproduce and extend\n\nExtract the ZIP with its directory structure. Python 3.12 and the standard library suffice:\n\n```text\npython experiments/records/doublet-placement/run.py --check\npython experiments/records/doublet-placement/check.py\n```\n\nThe producer stores input hashes, all 86 event slots, page lengths, exact zero-page expectation, simulation seeds, central ranges and inclusive rank counts. The independent checker extracts the runes another way, compares every event to the published [source-location ledger](#/wiki/doublets?section=counts), and recomputes the exact zero-page expectation from binomial coefficients. Run `--write` to regenerate the JSON and SVG. The analysis is conditional on the archived transcription; it does not settle uncertain glyphs or compare an independent complete transcription. For the boundary treatment of these same events, read the [separator audit](#/experiments/doublet-boundaries).\n",
  "article_path": "experiments/records/doublet-placement/article.md",
  "script_sha256": "1698649fcbfd2086f4870b27e2412677b57cb03e580ffc419a1587550b95d927",

  }
}

  "related": [
    "doublet-lag-profile",
    "doublet-context"
  ],
  "article": "## Finding\n\n**The 86 adjacent equal-rune pairs do not favor a position modulo 2 through 8 within their manuscript sections.** We reproduced the [published section-relative residue counts](https://github.com/Leo-Y-Zhang/LiberPrimusAnalysis/blob/a32bdc0e06ea58532fbaf4329acae4a0b1020513/results/lag_and_parity.txt) exactly. The strongest of seven adjusted concentration scores is **1.168** (modulo 2). In **4,316 of 5,000** controls, at least one of the seven scores is as high. That comparison retains the observed number of doublets in each section.\n\n![For modulo seven, the 86 doublets spread across all seven positions rather than clustering in one group.](experiments/records/doublet-section-residues/residues.svg)\n\n## What was tested\n\nA *doublet* is a pair of consecutive identical runes. The position used here is the **second rune's zero-based position within its section**. The nine unsolved sections are LP2-00–02, 03–07, 08–14, 15–22, 23–26, 27–32, 33–39, 40–53 and 54–55. We scanned every rune in those sections, found 86 doublets and counted their positions modulo 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7 and 8. All seven count vectors match the source test; for example, modulo 7 gives **7, 10, 12, 10, 15, 18, 14**.\n\nFor each modulus, the expected count accounts for how many eligible adjacent-pair positions of each residue exist in *each* section. The comparison then randomly places that section's **same number of doublet events** among its eligible positions. It repeats this 5,000 times and, in each trial, selects the strongest of the same seven moduli. Using the strongest result on both sides matters: after seeing seven residue plots, one will usually look uneven by chance. The statistic is chi-square divided by its degrees of freedom, so the different moduli can be compared on a common scale.\n\nThe control maximum has a median score of **1.858**; the manuscript's strongest score is **1.168**. The saved [results](experiments/records/doublet-section-residues/results.json) include every doublet position, expected count, seven observed score vectors and all 5,000 control maxima. A planted control keeps the nine section event counts but places them all on positions divisible by 7. Its adjusted modulo-7 score is **86.338**, far beyond the control range, confirming that a strong modular placement pattern would be visible.\n\n## Limit of the result\n\nThis does **not** rule out block ciphers or any general mechanism for suppressing adjacent repeats. It only finds no **section-position residue concentration** among the observed doublets for moduli 2–8 under this uniform-placement comparison. The comparison does not preserve possible clustering of events within sections, different word boundaries, or a cipher's expected position distribution. It also does not test sentence-relative positions: the public source's sentence-token rules cannot be reproduced exactly from the punctuation retained in this site's transcription. Those counts need a separate, pinned sentence-boundary inventory.\n\nTo reproduce offline, run `python experiments/records/doublet-section-residues/run.py --check` and `python experiments/records/doublet-section-residues/check.py`. The independent check extracts doublets again from the page text and verifies all seven residue vectors. No external files or network service are needed during replay.\n",
  "article_path": "experiments/records/doublet-section-residues/article.md",
  "script_sha256": "19138467d93babfcc2eff457a89349ddf27b32ea352218af0139127625d5346b",

    "id": "measurement",
    "label": "Manuscript measurement",
    "description": "Measures a stated feature or statistical comparison; it does not test a complete decoding rule."
  }
}

  "visuals": [
    {
      "path": "experiments/records/ea-difference-independence/differences.svg",
      "caption": "Counts for all 28 nonzero difference residues against the equal-count reference; the chart also reports the adjacent nonzero-difference match count."
    }

  "article": "# Are the nonzero differences independent under the EA-stalling model?\n\nThe [EA-frequency control](#/experiments/ea-frequency-control) compared the 86 LP2 doublets with decoded GP EA on solved pages and examined the index of coincidence (IoC) of successive ciphertext differences. This companion check asks what the **specific independent-nonzero-key version** of that equation predicts beyond the zero count. It keeps the observed zero positions and page boundaries fixed; it does not search for plaintext or keys.\n\nUnder `Cᵢ = Cᵢ₋₁ + Kᵢ(Pᵢ − 28) mod 29`, with each key independently uniform on 1–28 and independent of a fixed plaintext, every plaintext EA gives difference zero. For any other plaintext rune, multiplication by its nonzero offset permutes 1–28. Therefore, **conditional on the zero mask**, the other differences must be independent uniform draws from those 28 residues. This is a prediction of the declared key model, not of every running-sum cipher. A periodic, deterministic or nonuniform key need not have it.\n\n![Counts of the 28 nonzero difference residues on LP2-00–55, with their equal-count reference marked in red.](experiments/records/ea-difference-independence/differences.svg)\n\n## Input and two diagnostics\n\nRead archived LP2-00–55, including headings. Retain the 29 GP runes, discard other characters, and subtract each previous rune index from the next **within the same page** modulo 29. There are 12,901 differences: **86 zero** and **12,815 nonzero**. No pair is formed across a page boundary. The zero mask remains at its observed positions in all simulations.\n\nThe first diagnostic is the Pearson chi-square of the 28 nonzero residue counts against an equal-count reference. The expected count per residue is **12,815 / 28 ≈ 457.68**. The second counts equal neighboring nonzero differences. Both difference positions must be consecutive within one page; a zero between them breaks the comparison. That leaves **12,676 eligible pairs**, with **452.71** expected equalities if the nonzero draws are independent uniform residues.\n\n| Diagnostic | Observed | Central 95% of 2,000 conditional draws | Draws at least observed |\n| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |\n| 28-bin Pearson chi-square | 42.056 | 14.403–43.092 | 69 / 2,000 |\n| Equal neighboring nonzero differences | 432 / 12,676 | 412–492 | 1,685 / 2,000 |\n\nThe histogram statistic is near the high end of this seeded conditional reference. The order-sensitive count sits within it. The simulation uses seed `33012026`; every trial fills only nonzero-mask slots with independent draws from 1–28. In a positive control, those synthetic differences were accumulated into ciphertext and differenced again, recovering the simulated values exactly. The complete result stores all 28 observed bins, both tails of each simulated rank, source hashes and the plan.\n\n## The histogram is not independent evidence from the previous IoC\n\nLet `m = 12,815` and let `c₁ … c₂₈` be the nonzero difference counts. The chi-square is `28 Σ cᵣ² / m − m`. With the **86 zero differences fixed**, the full difference IoC has numerator `86 × 85 + Σ cᵣ(cᵣ − 1) = 86 × 85 + Σ cᵣ² − m` and a fixed denominator `12,901 × 12,900`. Both statistics are increasing functions of the same `Σ cᵣ²`. They rank every conditional simulated histogram in exactly the same order. The histogram makes the individual residues inspectable; its 69/2,000 upper rank is **not a second independent hint** alongside the earlier IoC result.\n\nNeighboring equality instead uses the **order** of nonzero differences. A page can keep every residue count—and thus the chi-square and IoC—while a rearrangement changes this adjacent-pair statistic. Here 432 equalities are below the 452.71 uniform expectation but inside the simulated central range. It would be a mistake to infer a periodic key, or its absence, from this one lag-one check.\n\n## What the result leaves open\n\nThe model and diagnostics were selected after the low doublet count and difference IoC were already known. These inclusive Monte Carlo ranks are descriptive and unadjusted for that selection or for examining two related summaries. They do not provide a prospective probability that the manuscript uses this cipher. A near-uniform residual distribution is compatible with many mechanisms; a small departure would challenge only the independently uniform nonzero-key version under these boundaries and transcription choices.\n\nNo plaintext EA positions have been verified, no key has been recovered, and no unknown page has been read. A deterministic key schedule, a clock that pauses on EA, word or page resets, changed rune mapping, and alternate transcription layers require separately declared tests. See the [doublet guide](#/wiki/doublets?section=ea-constraint) for the algebra and the [placement audit](#/experiments/doublet-placement) for the spatial distribution of the 86 zeros.\n\n## Reproduce\n\nExtract this experiment's ZIP without flattening folders. Python 3.12 and its standard library suffice:\n\n```text\npython experiments/records/ea-difference-independence/run.py --check\npython experiments/records/ea-difference-independence/check.py\n```\n\nThe producer reruns the 2,000 conditional draws and checks the saved JSON and SVG byte for byte. The independent checker extracts the Runic Unicode block with a different parser, verifies every source hash, recomputes the 28 bins and adjacent statistic, and calculates chi-square from an exact rational formula. Both use archived text, not a fresh manual rereading of the JPEGs. The [test plan](experiments/records/ea-difference-independence/plan.txt), [result data](experiments/records/ea-difference-independence/results.json) and [figure](experiments/records/ea-difference-independence/differences.svg) are available separately.\n",
  "article_path": "experiments/records/ea-difference-independence/article.md",

  "title": "Solved GP EA frequency versus unsolved LP2 doublets",
  "status": "published",
  "question": "Is the observed LP2 doublet rate compatible with the EA frequency in known decoded GP text under one proposed nonzero-key running-sum equation?",
  "summary": "Solved LP1 has 20 EA events in 2,782 within-page positions (0.719%); unsolved LP2 has 86 doublets in 12,901 positions (0.667%). Similarity is a necessary-frequency calibration, not cipher evidence. Erasing word boundaries spuriously raises solved LP1 EA to 31.",

  "visuals": [
    {
      "path": "experiments/records/ea-frequency-control/comparison.svg",
      "caption": "Solved LP1 decoded EA rate and unsolved LP2 doublet rate, each with its own numerator and denominator. Rate similarity is not confirmation of the running-sum model."
    }
  ],
  "article": "# Does EA occur often enough in solved text?\n\nA proposed running-sum explanation for the rare repeated runes makes a testable prediction: wherever its rule applies, two equal neighboring ciphertext runes would mark an EA rune in the hidden plaintext. This record asks whether EA occurs about as often in known readings as those repeats occur in unsolved LP2. Matching rates would satisfy one necessary condition; it would not recover plaintext or establish the cipher.\n\nThe proposed equation is `Cᵢ = Cᵢ₋₁ + Kᵢ(Pᵢ − 28) mod 29`. Here `C` is the ciphertext rune index, `P` the plaintext index, EA has index 28, and each key value `Kᵢ` must be nonzero. Under those conditions, a ciphertext doublet is equivalent to plaintext EA at that transition. This is an **exact property of the proposed equation**, not evidence that Liber Primus uses it.\n\nThe site's solved LP1 controls contain **20 EA runes in 2,782 within-page transition positions** (0.719%). Unsolved LP2-00–55 has **86 doublets in 12,901 within-page positions** (0.667%). If the solved LP1 rate were simply carried over, it would correspond to about **92.7 EA positions** at the unsolved length. That is close to 86, but many different ciphers or text-generation rules can produce the same marginal rate.\n\n![The EA rate in solved LP1 and doublet rate in unsolved LP2 shown as two horizontal bars, 0.719 and 0.667 percent.](experiments/records/ea-frequency-control/comparison.svg)\n\n| Source and measurement | Events | Positions | Rate |\n| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |\n| Solved LP1-01, 03–16: decoded GP EA | 20 | 2,782 | 0.719% |\n| Solved LP2-56–57: decoded GP EA | 0 | 178 | 0% |\n| Unsolved LP2-00–55: equal neighboring ciphertext runes | 86 | 12,901 | 0.667% |\n\nAs a scale for sampling variation, a 95% **Wilson score interval** for 20/2,782 is **0.466–1.108%** if those positions were independent draws with one fixed EA probability. The observed unsolved rate, 0.667%, lies inside that interval. The same calculation for 86/12,901 gives **0.540–0.822%**. These intervals overlap, but do not establish equal rates or a cipher: adjacent rune positions in prose are dependent, and the LP1 and LP2 sources are not random samples from one common process.\n\nTo reproduce the endpoints for either count, set `p = events / positions`, `n = positions`, and `z = 1.9599639845`. The endpoints are `[p + z²/(2n) ± z√(p(1−p)/n + z²/(4n²))] / [1 + z²/n]`. The page-resampling range below addresses a different source of variation. It also remains descriptive, not a probability distribution for unknown plaintext.\n\nThe two solved LP2 pages are short; their zero EA count is not a robust estimate for the much longer unsolved portion. The LP1 pages also differ in section and method from that portion. Resampling the 15 solved LP1 pages 10,000 times gives a descriptive range of roughly **54–132 EA positions** when each draw's rate is scaled to 12,901 positions. This shows how the small control set changes with page mix. It is **not** a predictive interval for unknown LP2 plaintext: the pages are section fragments, not independent random samples from a known common language process.\n\n## Why the spelling conversion matters\n\nThe known-reading source preserves actual decoded **GP rune indices** alongside their literal Latin labels. In all 17 solved control pages, removing row wraps and greedily taking the longest GP labels **within each printed token** reconstructs the stored index sequence exactly. That is a check on this literal source layer, not a license to parse normalized English the same way.\n\nIf all token boundaries are erased first, greedy parsing finds **31 EA labels** across the solved LP1 pages instead of the actual **20 EA runes**. The eleven extras are cross-word `E|A` joins such as `ONE | ALONG` and `STRUGGLE | AND`. The downloaded report lists all eleven. Even inside one ordinary English word, the letters `EA` do not prove the manuscript used the single EA rune: `REACT` could be segmented `R·EA·C·T` or `R·E·A·C·T`. In Gematria Primus, EA has prime value 109, while E plus A totals 67 + 97 = 164. Preserve original rune boundaries when testing a frequency or prime sum.\n\n## What about the difference IoC?\n\nSubtract each within-page ciphertext rune from the next modulo 29. This gives 12,901 differences, including 86 zeros. Their observed index of coincidence is **0.035325**. Under an additional idealized assumption—condition on exactly 86 zero differences, then draw all 12,815 nonzero values independently and uniformly from residues 1–28—the expected IoC is **0.035284**. In 2,000 seeded simulations, the central 95% interval was **0.035249–0.035326**; 54 trials reached or exceeded the observed value.\n\nSo 0.0353 is near the upper edge of this **conditional nonzero-uniform** reference: 54 of 2,000 draws were at least as high (2.7%). The observed value is still inside the central 95% simulation range. This is a mild tension with that one extra uniform-key assumption, not a test of the running-sum equation as a whole and not standalone confirmation. The reference was chosen after the zero deficit and IoC were known, and other features and baselines have also been examined. Shuffling the ciphertext runes within pages would change the zero count and ask a different question. Uniform nonzero differences are what independently uniform nonzero keys would imply at non-EA positions for this particular equation; other key schedules can behave differently.\n\nThe key layer explains the limitation. Write the observed difference as `Dᵢ = Cᵢ − Cᵢ₋₁`. For each **nonzero** Dᵢ and every one of the **28 non-EA plaintext symbols** Pᵢ, there is exactly one allowed nonzero key, `Kᵢ = Dᵢ(Pᵢ − 28)⁻¹ mod 29`. Thus an unconstrained key per position can fit *any* proposed non-EA plaintext at those positions. Conversely, an independently uniform nonzero key makes Dᵢ uniform on 1–28 regardless of how uneven the non-EA plaintext letter frequencies are. The conditional IoC can challenge that extra independent-uniform-key assumption; it cannot identify plaintext, establish EA at the 86 positions, or test an unspecified deterministic key schedule. **No fixed key schedule has been applied to unsolved LP2 in this record.** Doing so would be a different, stronger experiment with a declared generator and fixed parameters. Simply deleting the 86 zero differences leaves the same 12,815 nonzero values whose histogram is tested in the [companion record](#/experiments/ea-difference-independence). Deleting ciphertext runes instead creates new adjacencies and is a different operation.\n\nUnder the archived boundary rule, **22 of the 86 doublets cross a hyphen**. They are legitimate consecutive runes in the filtered stream but are not within-token repeats. If the proposed recurrence resets at word boundaries, those 22 edges no longer fall under its doublet⇔EA identity. If the key continues over boundaries, the identity still applies to the second rune of each edge, with the hyphen ignored by the cipher clock. The [separator audit](#/experiments/doublet-boundaries) lists every such position; the current count cannot decide which clock Cicada used.\n\nAll of these comparisons were designed after the low doublet count was known. A confirmatory version would need a key schedule, starting state, boundary/reset rule, rune mapping and success criterion fixed from evidence independent of the test output, then a prediction of untouched ciphertext or a verified plaintext passage. Merely changing an interval method or reserving positions after inspecting this corpus cannot turn the existing rate match into a prospective test.\n\nThe [doublet placement audit](#/experiments/doublet-placement) tests a different implication: whether the 86 candidate EA positions have unusual page counts or short gaps under explicit event-placement controls. Those controls also cannot establish a plaintext reading.\n\nThe [nonzero-difference companion](#/experiments/ea-difference-independence) keeps the observed zero positions fixed and checks residue balance and adjacent differences. Its 28-bin chi-square is algebraically the same information as the difference IoC reported above, so the two histogram summaries must not be counted as independent evidence.\n\n## Reproduce and limits\n\nExtract the experiment ZIP without flattening it. Python 3.12 and its standard library suffice:\n\n```text\npython experiments/records/ea-frequency-control/run.py --check\npython experiments/records/ea-frequency-control/check.py\n```\n\nThe producer hashes the known-reading extract, alphabet and all 56 unsolved text files. The independent checker recounts decoded EA indices, reconstructs literal labels, verifies the cross-word joins, and recalculates the exact difference IoC. The source extract uses established decoded readings and a documented LP1-10 correction; this experiment is not a fresh image audit. It cannot tell whether the 86 doublets are plaintext EA, nor recover the nonzero key sequence. See [the doublet guide](#/wiki/doublets?section=ea-constraint) for the equation and its assumptions, and the [boundary audit](#/experiments/doublet-boundaries) for where the 86 pairs sit relative to stored separators.\n",
  "article_path": "experiments/records/ea-frequency-control/article.md",
  "script_sha256": "dda6228d312ac99db8c671f82c34bac5613c78d3a416364975c223bfca7c449e",

  "article": "# Historical Emerson book-cipher control\n\n## Purpose and what this does not test\n\nA book cipher needs a source edition and counting conventions, not just a book title. This record reproduces the documented 2014 opening-image coordinates against the frozen Emerson Self-Reliance PDF derivative. It gives newcomers a working control and a trace they can inspect before proposing new book-cipher experiments.\n\n**The answer was known before this rerun.** This is a historical replication, not blind discovery, an independent confirmation of source selection, or a decipherment of an unsolved manuscript page. No hidden-service address was visited.\n\n## Frozen plan and prior reconstruction history\n\nThe rerun plan and wrapper were committed as `1f67f70` before this execution. Source files, the existing lookup script and the known result were hashed in the plan. An earlier reconstruction had corrected the treatment of embedded verse after inspecting mismatches: the verse remains inside prose paragraph 36 rather than creating extra paragraphs. That earlier adjustment is disclosed in the existing evidence manifest and is not presented here as a rule discovered independently.\n\nThe PDF is the contemporary snapshot linked in the historical walkthrough. Its hash is fixed, but the original creator's exact edition is not authenticated by this reproduction.\n\n## Counting conventions\n\nRe-extract the pinned PDF with pypdf 6.19.0 in layout mode. Begin at the first prose paragraph, exclude numeric page footers, and use four-space prose indentation to begin paragraphs. Seven-space verse remains in its surrounding paragraph. Apply Unicode NFKC normalization and join wrapped lines according to the stored extraction rule. All 50 extracted paragraphs must match the frozen derivative.\n\nCoordinates are one-based paragraph:sentence:word:letter positions. Sentences split at `.`, `!` and `?`; words split on whitespace with edge punctuation removed; only ASCII letters count inside the selected word. Single-character entries are copied literally. These are the documented reconstruction conventions, not a universal natural-language sentence parser.\n\n## Result\n\nThe complete trace matches the archived control. Fifteen coordinate lookups and seven literal characters reconstruct:\n\n```\nauqgnxjtvdbll3pv.onion\n```\n\nThis is a historical output string. Reproducing it says nothing about any current service at that name. The supported claim is only that these exact inputs and rules reproduce the recorded trace.\n\n## Complete coordinate trace\n\n| Entry | Printed PDF page | Selected word | Output |\n| --- | --- | --- | --- |\n| 1:2:3:1 | 1 | always | a |\n| 3:3:13:5 | 2 | genius | u |\n| 45:5:2:3 | 19 | acquires | q |\n| 20:3:20:5 | 9 | among | g |\n| 8:3:8:6 | 5 | action | n |\n| 48:5:14:2 | 20 | experience | x |\n| 21:13:4:1 | 9 | justice | j |\n| 25:1:7:4 | 12 | truth | t |\n| 15:9:3:4 | 7 | above | v |\n| 1:1:16:3 | 1 | and | d |\n| 4:3:3:1 | 2 | being | b |\n| 8:3:26:4 | 5 | daily | l |\n| 47:3:3:5 | 19 | equality | l |\n| 3 | Literal | Copied directly | 3 |\n| 13:2:5:4 | 6 | corpse | p |\n| 1:4:16:4 | 1 | private | v |\n| . | Literal | Copied directly | . |\n| o | Literal | Copied directly | o |\n| n | Literal | Copied directly | n |\n| i | Literal | Copied directly | i |\n| o | Literal | Copied directly | o |\n| n | Literal | Copied directly | n |\n\nThe first coordinate, 1:2:3:1, selects the third word of the second sentence in paragraph 1: `always`. Its first letter is `a`. The JSON output includes each full selected sentence, so a reader can check the counting rather than trusting the final string alone.\n\n## Reproduce from files\n\nUse Python 3.12.10 and pypdf 6.19.0. Install the exact dependency in your preferred environment:\n\n```\npython -m pip install pypdf==6.19.0\npython experiments/records/emerson-book-cipher-control/run.py --check\n```\n\nDependency installation needs package access; the actual experiment makes no network request. The wrapper checks every frozen input hash, invokes the existing reproduction script with `--check-pdf`, compares all 50 paragraphs, and checks the complete output trace. It then compares the new report with the saved one. Missing dependencies or changed inputs fail visibly.\n\nTo save a separate report:\n\n```\npython experiments/records/emerson-book-cipher-control/run.py --output my-emerson-control.json\n```\n\nExisting output files are never overwritten. [Download the complete trace](experiments/records/emerson-book-cipher-control/results.json). [Download the pinned PDF](exports/sources/emerson-self-reliance.pdf) and [paragraph derivative](exports/sources/emerson-paragraphs.json). The [coordinate payload](exports/steganography/opening-2014.body.txt) is the extracted message body; extraction and signature verification are separate steps described in the opening-image guide.\n\nFor a standard-library-only replay of the frozen paragraphs, run `python scripts/reproduce_emerson.py` without `--check-pdf`. That shorter check does not re-extract the PDF and must not be reported as having done so.\n\n## Retest and review\n\nCodex ran the PDF reconstruction and lookup twice on 20 October 2026. Both produced the same 50 paragraphs and identical complete trace. No counting rule or source changed during this rerun. The diagram was generated afterward from the saved first lookup. Human review remains pending, and the lookup implementation is the existing historical reproduction code rather than a newly independent decoder.\n\n## Family and future variants\n\nA different edition, paragraph convention or source text needs a separate variant with the exact change recorded. An attempt to apply a book cipher to an unsolved LP2 page also needs an independently defined source of coordinates and a success criterion. This historical control is useful for checking an implementation; it does not establish that such a transfer has already been tested.\n\nSee [book-cipher conventions](#/wiki/book-ciphers), [Emerson and the historical source](#/wiki/emerson-self-reliance), and [the opening image](#/wiki/opening-2014).\n",

  "article": "# Does the preserved Emerson text work as an LP2 running key?\n\nUnder **one fully specified additive rule**, the tested LP2 pages do not show a convincing Emerson-key opening or continuation. We searched every **43,325 contiguous offsets** of the archived *Self-Reliance* extract for each of LP2-00, LP2-31 and LP2-54. The best 96-rune openings score near maxima from eight complete searches using shuffled versions of the same source letters. Their next 96 runes remain far below a planted known-reading control. This does not exclude other running-key rules, source editions, alphabets or page positions.\n\n![Opening and held-out continuation scores for Emerson and shuffled-source searches](experiments/records/emerson-running-key/search-scores.svg)\n\n## Why this source and what rule was frozen\n\nEmerson's *Self-Reliance* is a documented source for a **2014 book-coordinate cipher**, reproduced separately in the [historical control](#/experiments/emerson-book-cipher-control). That history makes it a concrete candidate to test; a coordinate cipher does not establish a running key for LP2. We used the site's preserved **50-paragraph PDF derivative**, not an authenticated creator edition. Its original file, extraction convention and SHA-256 are described in the [Emerson source guide](#/wiki/emerson-self-reliance).\n\nJoin the 50 stored paragraphs with spaces, uppercase, and retain ASCII A–Z. The result has **43,516 letters**. Map A to 0 through Z to 25. For each LP2 page, take its first 192 archived alphabet runes in order, including headings. At each offset, subtract successive source-letter values from rune indices modulo 29; the source does not wrap, and punctuation advances neither stream. This is deliberately a Latin-letter-to-rune numeric key, not a claim that Emerson's prose was written in Gematria Primus.\n\nScore the first **96 decoded runes** after concatenating their canonical Latin labels. The score is the mean base-10 log probability of overlapping four-letter groups under the pinned [English quadgram model](#/experiments/english-scorer-controls); unseen groups receive count 0.01. Select the highest first-window score, breaking ties toward the lowest source offset. Only then score the **next 96 runes** at that same offset. Search eight deterministic full-stream letter shuffles with exactly the same offset budget and selection rule. Those controls preserve the source's letter counts while breaking its order. The [plan](experiments/records/emerson-running-key/plan.json) fixes these choices and hashes every input.\n\n## Complete search maxima\n\nHigher scores are more English-like under this exact scorer. The shuffle ranges below contain the **best selected candidate from each complete shuffled-source search**, not scores of arbitrary unselected offsets.\n\n| Target | Best Emerson offset | First 96 | Eight shuffle maxima | Next 96 at chosen offset | Shuffle continuations |\n| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |\n| LP2-00 | 19,692 | −6.364 | −6.372 to −6.143 | −7.575 | −7.807 to −7.054 |\n| LP2-31 | 1,162 | −6.353 | −6.444 to −6.218 | −7.368 | −7.875 to −7.306 |\n| LP2-54 | 21,646 | −6.462 | −6.536 to −6.255 | −6.817 | −7.754 to −6.997 |\n\nThe LP2-54 continuation scores higher than all eight shuffled-source continuations. That observation is retained, not dismissed: there are only eight controls, its first window was not stronger than their maxima, and its continuation score is still far below the known-reading plant. These values are **descriptive**, not a calibrated p-value or an English-language decision threshold. The [full result](experiments/records/emerson-running-key/results.json) preserves the top five offsets and both decoded windows for every search, so a reader can inspect the candidate text rather than rely on one number.\n\n## Did the search have a fair chance to find a real key?\n\nAs a positive control, take the first 192 **decoded** rune indices of LP1-06, add the same Emerson key beginning at zero-based offset **3,301**, and search the resulting synthetic ciphertext without telling the search its offset. The complete 43,325-offset search ranks **3,301 first**, recovers the known indices exactly there, and scores **−4.096** on the first 96 and **−3.883** on the next 96. This proves the pipeline can recover a planted instance of the specified rule at this length. It does not establish its power for every possible plaintext or source text.\n\nThe scorer itself has documented language limits: it can reject meaningful Welsh, for example, while accepting some non-English text. Canonical rune labels also differ from ordinary English spelling. A low score therefore cannot exclude a non-English plaintext or every English representation. The result only weakens this **single Emerson / A–Z shifts / subtractive modulo-29 / page-opening** variant. A proposal with a different source conversion, offset reset, interrupted clock, or selected passage is a different search and must count those choices.\n\n## Reproduce\n\nWith Python 3 standard library, from the repository root or extracted [experiment ZIP](downloads/experiments/emerson-running-key.zip):\n\n```text\npython experiments/records/emerson-running-key/run.py --check\npython experiments/records/emerson-running-key/check.py\npython experiments/records/emerson-running-key/plot.py --check\n```\n\nThe producer checks all source hashes and replays every complete offset search. The independent checker reconstructs the source, shuffles, rune streams and planted ciphertext; it scores by counted quadgrams rather than the producer's sliding sum, and verifies every maximum, top-five list and holdout. The plotter checks the published figure. No API, model download or network call is needed.\n",
